name: FCSB
content:
FCSB is one of the most successful and popular football clubs in Romania. Founded in 1947 in Bucharest as the army’s football team, the club became famous under the name Steaua București and dominated Romanian football for decades. FCSB achieved international recognition in 1986 when it won the European Cup, becoming the first club from Eastern Europe to lift the trophy after defeating Barcelona in the final. The team also won the UEFA Super Cup in 1987 and reached another European Cup final in 1989.

Domestically, the club has won numerous Romanian league titles and cup competitions, establishing itself as a dominant force in the country’s football history. FCSB has consistently competed in European tournaments and has produced many legendary Romanian players over the years, including Gheorghe Hagi and Marius Lăcătuș. The club is known for its passionate supporters, historic rivalries with Dinamo București and Rapid București, and its strong presence in Romanian football culture.

In recent decades, the club has been involved in major legal disputes regarding the Steaua name, logo, and historical identity. After a series of court decisions, the team officially changed its name from FC Steaua București to FCSB in 2017. Despite the controversy surrounding the ownership of the club’s historical honors, FCSB has remained one of the strongest teams in Romania and continues to compete regularly in domestic and European competitions.

name: FC Dinamo București
content:
FC Dinamo București is one of the most historic and successful football clubs in Romania. Founded in 1948 in Bucharest, the club quickly became one of the dominant forces in Romanian football during the communist era. Dinamo developed a fierce rivalry with Steaua București, and matches between the two clubs became known as the “Eternal Derby,” one of the biggest rivalries in Eastern European football. The club has traditionally been associated with the Ministry of Internal Affairs and has built a large and passionate fanbase over the decades.

Dinamo has won numerous Romanian league titles and domestic cups, establishing itself as one of the country’s most decorated teams. The club also achieved notable success in European competitions, especially during the 1980s, when it reached the semi-finals of the European Cup in the 1983–84 season. Throughout its history, Dinamo produced many important Romanian footballers and regularly contributed players to the national team, helping shape Romanian football at both domestic and international levels.

In recent years, the club has faced financial and sporting difficulties, including relegation struggles and ownership instability. Despite these challenges, Dinamo remains one of the most recognized football institutions in Romania, with loyal supporters and a strong historical identity. The team continues to play an important role in Romanian football culture and is still considered one of the country’s traditional giants.

name: CFR Cluj
content:
CFR Cluj is one of the most successful modern football clubs in Romania, based in the city of Cluj-Napoca. Founded in 1907, the club has a long history connected to the railway community, with “CFR” standing for “Căile Ferate Române,” the Romanian Railways. Although the club spent many years outside the top division during the twentieth century, it rose to national prominence in the 2000s and became one of the dominant forces in Romanian football.

The club won its first Romanian league title in the 2007–08 season and quickly established itself as a regular challenger for domestic trophies. CFR Cluj achieved notable success in European competitions, competing in the UEFA Champions League and Europa League against major European clubs. The team became known for its disciplined style of play, experienced squads, and strong performances in important matches. Over the years, the club has won multiple Liga I titles and Romanian Cups, becoming one of the most decorated Romanian teams of the modern era.

CFR Cluj has also played an important role in developing football in Transylvania and increasing the competitiveness of Romanian football outside Bucharest. The club’s rivalry with Universitatea Cluj, known as the Cluj Derby, is one of the most intense rivalries in Romanian football. Supported by passionate fans and backed by consistent domestic success, CFR Cluj continues to be a major presence in Romanian football and a frequent participant in European competitions.

name: FC Venus București
content:
FC Venus București was one of the most important football clubs in Romania during the interwar period. Founded in 1914 in Bucharest, the club quickly became a dominant force in Romanian football and earned the nickname “The Black Devils” because of its black kits. Venus played its home matches at the famous Venus Stadium, which was considered one of the most modern stadiums in Romania at the time and was among the first in the country to host matches under floodlights.

The club enjoyed enormous success before World War II, winning multiple Romanian championship titles and establishing itself as one of the strongest teams in the country. Venus București was particularly successful during the 1930s and became known for its attractive football and strong organization. The team also participated in the Mitropa Cup, one of Europe’s earliest international club competitions, where it faced major Central European clubs. Despite its domestic dominance, Venus never managed to win the Romanian Cup, losing several important matches against local rivals Rapid București.

After the rise of the communist regime in Romania, the club was forced to merge with a state institution and was eventually dissolved in 1949. Its historic stadium was later demolished, and the club disappeared from Romanian football for decades. In 2014, Venus București was officially re-founded and returned to the lower divisions of Romanian football, preserving the legacy of one of the country’s greatest historic clubs. Even today, Venus remains an important symbol of early Romanian football history.

name: FC UTA Arad
content:
FC UTA Arad is one of the most historic football clubs in Romania, based in the city of Arad near the country’s western border. The club was founded in 1945 by businessman Francisc von Neuman, who modeled the team after English football clubs and provided it with modern facilities for the time. UTA quickly became one of the strongest teams in Romanian football and earned national recognition during the postwar period. The club’s name originally stood for “Uzinele Textile Arad,” reflecting its connection to the local textile industry.

UTA Arad enjoyed its golden era during the 1960s and 1970s, winning several Romanian league titles and establishing itself as a serious competitor at both domestic and European levels. One of the club’s most famous achievements came in the 1970–71 European Cup, when UTA eliminated the Dutch champions Feyenoord, who had won the European Cup the previous season. The team became known for its disciplined football, talented Romanian players, and strong support from local fans. Throughout its history, UTA developed a fierce rivalry with Poli Timișoara, creating one of the traditional regional derbies in Romanian football.

After periods of financial difficulties and relegation, the club spent years outside the top division before eventually returning to Liga I in the modern era. UTA continues to be viewed as an important symbol of football tradition in western Romania and maintains a loyal fanbase. The club now plays at the modern Stadionul Francisc von Neuman, named after its founder, and remains one of the most respected historic teams in Romanian football.

name: Chinezul Timișoara
content:
Chinezul Timișoara was one of the greatest football clubs in early Romanian football history. Founded in 1910 in the city of Timișoara, the club became famous during the 1920s when it dominated the national championship. Chinezul won six consecutive Romanian league titles between 1921 and 1927, a remarkable achievement that established the club as the strongest team in the country during that era. The club’s name, which means “The Chinese,” came from a local commercial association and became widely recognized throughout Romanian football.

The team was known for its modern style of play, strong organization, and talented players, helping shape the development of football in Romania during the interwar period. Chinezul Timișoara regularly defeated the leading clubs of the time and became one of the first Romanian teams to gain international attention through friendly matches against foreign opponents. Its dominance during the 1920s made the club an important symbol of football progress in western Romania and helped increase the popularity of the sport across the country.

After its golden era, the club gradually declined due to financial problems and increased competition from other Romanian teams. By the 1940s, Chinezul had lost its position among the country’s elite clubs, and it eventually disappeared from top-level football. Despite its decline, Chinezul Timișoara remains an iconic name in Romanian football history because of its record-breaking achievements and its major role in the early development of the sport in Romania.

name: CS Universitatea Craiova
content:
CS Universitatea Craiova is one of the most famous football clubs in Romania, based in the city of Craiova in the historical region of Oltenia. Founded in 1948 as part of the local university sports organization, the club became a major force in Romanian football during the 1970s and 1980s. Universitatea Craiova gained national popularity for its attacking style of play and talented generation of players, earning the nickname “The Champion of a Great Love” because of the passionate support it received from fans across the region.

The club enjoyed its greatest success during the late 1970s and early 1980s, winning several Romanian league titles and domestic cups. Universitatea Craiova also became the first Romanian club to reach the semi-finals of a major European competition when it advanced to the UEFA Cup semi-finals in the 1982–83 season. The team was known as “Craiova Maxima” during this golden era and featured many important Romanian internationals who helped raise the profile of Romanian football in Europe.

After the fall of communism, the club experienced financial and organizational difficulties, including legal disputes and periods outside top-level football. Despite these challenges, Universitatea Craiova has remained one of the most beloved clubs in Romania, supported by a passionate fanbase and strong regional identity. The team continues to compete in Liga I and is considered one of the traditional giants of Romanian football, with an important place in the country’s sporting history.

name: FC Petrolul Ploiești
content:
FC Petrolul Ploiești is one of the most traditional football clubs in Romania, based in the city of Ploiești. The club was originally founded in 1924 in Bucharest through the merger of two local teams and initially played under the name Juventus București. After several name changes and relocations in the post-war period, the club permanently settled in Ploiești in 1952, gradually building its identity around the local oil industry, which inspired its later name “Petrolul.”

The club experienced its golden era in the 1950s and 1960s, when it became one of the strongest teams in Romanian football. During this period, Petrolul won multiple national league titles and established itself as a consistent contender in domestic competitions. The team also earned respect in European football, participating in various continental tournaments and achieving notable results against strong international opponents. Known for its yellow and blue colors, the club gained the nickname “The Yellow Wolves” and developed a passionate fanbase.

In modern times, Petrolul has faced financial difficulties, relegations, and even restructuring, but it has managed to return to top-level Romanian football. The club also experienced a supporter-led revival after bankruptcy issues, which helped preserve its identity and traditions. Today, Petrolul Ploiești remains an important symbol of Romanian football heritage, with a strong local following and a reputation as one of the country’s historic clubs.

name: FC Ripensia Timișoara
content:
FC Ripensia Timișoara is one of the most historic football clubs in Romania, founded in 1928 in Timișoara. It was created by Dr. Cornel Lazăr and became the first professional football club in the country, which made it highly influential in the early development of Romanian football. The club quickly built a strong squad using players from other local teams and established itself as a pioneer of professional football in Romania. Its name comes from “Dacia Ripensis,” a reference to a Roman province, and it became a symbol of innovation in Romanian sport.

During the 1930s, Ripensia Timișoara experienced a golden era, dominating Romanian football before World War II. The club won multiple national league titles and also secured Romanian Cup victories, becoming one of the strongest teams in the country at that time. Ripensia was known for its professional organization, modern approach to training, and talented players, and it also participated in early European competitions like the Mitropa Cup, where it faced some of the strongest Central European clubs.

After World War II, the club suffered from financial difficulties and political changes, which led to its decline and eventual disappearance in 1948. For decades, Ripensia remained inactive until it was re-founded in 2012, starting again from the lower divisions of Romanian football. Since its revival, the club has gradually climbed back through the league system and rebuilt its identity, becoming a respected symbol of Romanian football tradition and history.

name: FC Rapid București
content:
FC Rapid București is one of the most popular and historic football clubs in Romania, based in the Giulești district of Bucharest. The club was founded in 1923 by railway workers under the name Asociația Culturală și Sportivă CFR, and it quickly became known as “the Railwaymen.” Rapid developed a strong working-class identity and built a reputation for passionate support, with one of the most loyal fanbases in Romanian football.

The club’s golden periods came across several eras, especially in the mid-20th century and again in the late 1990s and early 2000s. Rapid has won multiple Romanian league titles and has been particularly successful in the Romanian Cup, where it has historically been one of the most dominant teams. The club also achieved notable results in European competitions, including reaching the quarter-finals of major UEFA tournaments, which strengthened its reputation beyond Romania.

Rapid is also famous for its intense rivalries, especially with FCSB, Dinamo București, and Petrolul Ploiești, with matches between these teams being among the most emotional in Romanian football. In recent history, the club faced financial problems and even bankruptcy issues, but it was later re-established and returned to top-level football. Today, Rapid București remains a symbol of tradition, resilience, and strong fan culture in Romanian sport.

name: FC Argeș Pitești
content:
FC Argeș Pitești is a Romanian football club based in the city of Pitești, in Argeș County. The club was originally founded in 1953 under the name Dinamo Pitești and made its debut in Romania’s top division in the early 1960s. In 1967, it adopted the name FC Argeș and gradually built its identity around strong local tradition and one of Romania’s most respected football academies. The club is closely associated with legendary Romanian player Nicolae Dobrin, who became its most iconic figure.

The most successful period in FC Argeș history came in the 1970s, when the club won two Romanian league titles in 1972 and 1979. During this era, Argeș was considered one of the strongest teams in the country, regularly competing at the top level and producing talented players for the Romanian national team. The club also participated in European competitions, where it faced strong international opponents and gained valuable experience on the continental stage. Its home matches are traditionally played at the Nicolae Dobrin Stadium, named after its greatest legend.

After its golden years, FC Argeș experienced financial difficulties, relegations, and even periods of instability that led to restructuring and temporary setbacks. Despite these challenges, the club was re-established and managed to return to professional football, gradually climbing back to higher divisions. Today, FC Argeș remains an important symbol of Romanian football history, known for its tradition, strong regional identity, and contribution to developing talented players.

name: Colentina AC
content:
Colentina AC was a Romanian football club based in Bucharest, founded in 1909. It was one of the early football teams in the country and represented the Colentina cotton factory community, which gave the club its industrial and working-class identity. The team was among the pioneers of organized football in Romania during the early 20th century, a period when the sport was still developing in the country.

The club achieved significant success before World War I, becoming one of the strongest teams in Romanian football at the time. It won the Romanian national championship twice, in 1912–13 and 1913–14, which marked the peak of its sporting achievements. During this period, the squad was largely composed of English players working in Romania, which influenced its playing style and helped the team dominate early competitions.

After the First World War, Colentina AC gradually declined as many foreign players left the country and the club lost its competitive strength. It continued to participate at lower levels of Romanian football for several decades, but never returned to its early dominance. The club was eventually dissolved in 1947, leaving behind a legacy as one of the founding-era champions of Romanian football.

name: Olympia București
content:
Olympia București was one of the earliest football clubs in Romania and a pioneer of organized football in the country. The club was founded in 1904 in Bucharest by a group of Romanian and foreign enthusiasts, making it one of the first football teams established in the capital. It quickly became an important symbol of the early development of the sport in Romania and played a key role in introducing structured competition.

In the early years of Romanian football, Olympia București was among the strongest teams and achieved significant success. The club won the first editions of the Romanian national championship, dominating the pre–World War I period and helping shape the foundations of domestic football competitions. During this era, football in Romania was still developing, and Olympia stood out as one of the leading clubs in establishing competitive standards.

After its early dominance, the club gradually declined following World War I, losing its leading position to emerging teams in Bucharest and other cities. It continued to exist in various forms and lower competitions for several decades, but it never returned to its former strength. Eventually, Olympia București was dissolved in 1946, leaving behind an important legacy as one of the founding clubs of Romanian football and a key part of its early history.

name: FC Universitatea Cluj
content:
FC Universitatea Cluj is a Romanian football club based in Cluj-Napoca, founded in 1919 by students and academics under the guidance of doctor Iuliu Hațieganu. From its earliest years, the club became closely linked with the local university environment, which is why it is often called “the Students.” Universitatea Cluj is one of the traditional teams of Transylvania and has built a strong identity around education, culture, and regional pride.

Throughout its history, the club has spent many seasons in Romania’s top division but has never managed to win the national league title. However, it has had moments of success, including reaching several Romanian Cup finals and winning the competition in the 1964–65 season. The team is known for its long-standing presence in Romanian football and its role as one of the most important clubs outside Bucharest, often representing Transylvania in national competitions.

Universitatea Cluj is also famous for its passionate supporters, known as “Șepcile Roșii” (The Red Caps), and for its rivalry with CFR Cluj, which is one of the strongest modern rivalries in Romanian football. Despite periods of relegation and financial instability, the club has repeatedly returned to the top tier and remains an important symbol of tradition and identity in Romanian sport. Today, it continues to compete in Liga I and is considered one of the most respected historic clubs in the country.

name: FC Astra Giurgiu
content:
FC Astra Giurgiu was a Romanian football club based in Giurgiu, known for its relatively recent rise to prominence compared to many traditional teams in the country. The club was originally founded in 1921 in Ploiești as Astra Română, representing workers from the local oil industry. For most of its early history, Astra played in the lower divisions of Romanian football and had little national impact. Over time, however, it slowly developed and began building a more competitive squad.

The club’s breakthrough came in the late 1990s and especially during the 2000s, when it rose through the Romanian league system and established itself in the top division. A major turning point occurred after the club was taken over by businessman Ioan Niculae, which provided financial stability and allowed Astra to become a competitive force in Liga I. In 2012, the team relocated from Ploiești to Giurgiu, where it continued its development and eventually reached the peak of its success.

Astra Giurgiu’s greatest achievement came in the 2015–16 season when it won its first and only Romanian league title. The club also won the Romanian Cup and Supercup and made notable appearances in European competitions, including strong performances in the UEFA Europa League. However, after financial difficulties and loss of support, the club declined rapidly in the early 2020s and was eventually dissolved in 2022, ending its short but impactful modern history in Romanian football.

name: FC Unirea Urziceni
content:
FC Unirea Urziceni was a Romanian football club based in the small city of Urziceni in Ialomița County. The club was founded in 1954 and spent most of its early history in the lower divisions of Romanian football with little national impact. For decades, it remained a modest provincial team, changing names several times and operating with limited resources before eventually stabilizing under the name Unirea.

The club’s rise began in the 2000s after being taken over by businessman Dumitru Bucșaru, who invested in infrastructure, coaching, and experienced players. Unirea quickly climbed through the league system, reaching Liga I for the first time in 2006 and surprising Romanian football with strong performances. Under coach Dan Petrescu, the team developed into a highly organized and competitive side, culminating in its greatest achievement: winning the Romanian league title in the 2008–09 season, an extraordinary success for a small-town club.

After its championship success, Unirea Urziceni competed in European competitions, including the UEFA Champions League, but financial instability soon followed. In 2010, the club’s main investor withdrew support, forcing the sale of key players and leading to a rapid decline in results. The team was relegated and, unable to sustain operations, was officially dissolved in 2011, ending one of the most dramatic short-lived success stories in Romanian football history.

name: Unirea Tricolor București
content:
Unirea Tricolor București was a Romanian football club based in Bucharest, formed in 1914 originally under the name Tricolor București. It started as a team created by students in the Obor district and quickly became one of the early important clubs in Romanian football. After World War I, the club grew stronger and became one of the competitive sides in the early national championships, helping shape the development of organized football in Romania. It was also known for contributing players and ideas to the early Romanian football system.

In 1926, Tricolor merged with another local club, Unirea, forming Unirea Tricolor București. During the interwar period, the club became one of the stronger teams in the country and even won the Romanian national championship in the 1940–41 season. It also produced several notable players and remained an important presence in Bucharest football, competing regularly at the top level and contributing to the competitive growth of Romanian football before World War II.

After World War II, the club’s identity changed dramatically due to political restructuring in Romania. In 1948, it was taken over by the Ministry of Internal Affairs and merged into the newly created Dinamo system, becoming part of Dinamo București’s structure. The original Unirea Tricolor name disappeared, and after a series of relocations and reorganizations, the club ceased to exist as an independent entity by the late 1950s, leaving behind a legacy as one of the important early Romanian football clubs.

name: CSM Reșița
content:
CSM Reșița is one of the most historic football clubs in Romania, based in the city of Reșița in the Banat region. The club was founded in 1926 and has a long tradition connected to the local industrial background, particularly the steel and machinery factories that shaped the city. In its early decades, the club quickly became one of the important teams in Romanian football, representing a strong working-class identity and building a reputation as a competitive side in national competitions.

The greatest success in the club’s history came in the early 1930s, when Reșița won the Romanian national championship in the 1930–31 season. The team also finished as runners-up the following year, confirming its status as one of the strongest clubs in the country at that time. In 1954, the club added another major achievement by winning the Romanian Cup, further strengthening its place in Romanian football history. Over the years, Reșița also spent many seasons in the top division and was known for its resilience and strong regional identity.

In the modern era, CSM Reșița experienced financial difficulties, reorganizations, and periods in lower divisions, including spells in amateur and third-tier football. Despite these challenges, the club has managed to rebuild itself and return to higher levels of competition, supported by a loyal fanbase known for its strong local pride. Today, CSM Reșița continues to be an important symbol of football tradition in western Romania and remains one of the most historic clubs in the country.

name: CS Colțea Brașov
content:
CS Colțea Brașov was a Romanian football club based in Brașov, founded in 1920 as a branch of the Bucharest club Colțea. It was created by former players of Colțea București and quickly became one of the strongest provincial teams in early Romanian football. Despite its short existence, the club made a strong impact during the interwar period, competing in the national championships and establishing itself as a competitive side in the country’s developing football scene.

The club’s most successful moment came in the late 1920s, when it reached the top level of Romanian football and achieved major results. After reaching the national final in 1926–27, Colțea Brașov won the Romanian championship in the 1927–28 season, marking the greatest achievement in its history. This victory was particularly significant as it ended the dominance of stronger teams of the era and confirmed Colțea as one of the leading clubs in Romania at the time.

After its brief golden period, the club declined and was dissolved in 1931, disappearing from Romanian football for many decades. It was later re-founded in 2015, starting again in the lower divisions with a focus on youth development and rebuilding its identity. Today, CS Colțea Brașov is remembered mainly for its historic championship title and its role in the early evolution of football in Romania.

name: FCV Farul Constanța
content:
FCV Farul Constanța is a Romanian football club based in the city of Constanța, on the Black Sea coast. The club has its origins in 1920 and went through several name changes and reorganizations over the decades before becoming known as Farul Constanța. It is one of the most traditional teams in Romanian football from outside the capital and is strongly connected to the maritime identity of the region.

For much of its history, Farul competed in Romania’s top division but rarely challenged for major trophies, with its best league finish being mid-table and its standout achievement in the Cupa României being a final appearance in 2005. The club became better known for developing players and maintaining a stable presence in Liga I rather than winning titles. In 2021, Farul merged with Viitorul Constanța, combining resources and strengthening its long-term ambitions under the leadership associated with Gheorghe Hagi.

After the merger, the club experienced a major revival and quickly became one of the strongest sides in Romanian football again. Farul went on to achieve its greatest success by winning the Romanian league title in the 2022–23 season, marking a historic milestone for the club. Today, FCV Farul Constanța is considered a modern success story in Romanian football, blending tradition with a strong academy system and renewed competitive strength.

name: FC Viitorul Constanța
content:
FC Viitorul Constanța was a Romanian football club based in Ovidiu, near Constanța, founded in 2009 by former Romanian international Gheorghe Hagi. The club was created with a strong focus on youth development and quickly became known for producing talented young players through its academy. From its early years, Viitorul worked its way up the Romanian football pyramid, starting from the lower divisions and steadily achieving promotion to higher levels.

Viitorul reached Romania’s top division, Liga I, in 2012 and gradually established itself as a competitive side, despite being one of the youngest clubs in the league. The team’s playing philosophy emphasized technical football and the integration of academy graduates into the first team. Its most successful period came under Gheorghe Hagi’s leadership, when the club developed a reputation as a “talent factory” and began consistently competing in the upper half of the league table.

The club achieved its greatest success in the 2016–17 season, when it won the Romanian league title, a major milestone for such a young organization. This victory also brought qualification for European competitions, marking Viitorul’s rise to national prominence. In 2021, Viitorul merged with FC Farul Constanța, effectively ending its independent existence and forming a stronger unified club that continued under the Farul identity.

name: ASC Oțelul Galați
content:
ASC Oțelul Galați is a Romanian football club based in the city of Galați, strongly connected to the local steel industry. The club was founded in 1964 and originally represented workers from the Galați steelworks, which also inspired its name, “Oțelul,” meaning “The Steel.” For many years, the team developed gradually through the lower divisions before becoming a stable presence in Romanian professional football.

The club reached Romania’s top division, Liga I, in 1986 and later established itself as a competitive side in the national championship. Its greatest success came in the 2010–11 season when Oțelul won its first and only Romanian league title, a historic achievement for the club and its region. This success was followed by participation in European competitions, including the UEFA Champions League group stage, marking the peak of its modern era.

After its championship period, Oțelul faced serious financial problems, including insolvency and organizational collapse in the mid-2010s. The club was re-founded by supporters and restarted from the lower leagues, gradually rebuilding its status in Romanian football. Today, ASC Oțelul Galați competes again at a high level and is regarded as a symbol of resilience, representing both the industrial heritage of Galați and the passion of its supporters.

name: Româno-Americană București
content:
Româno-Americană București was one of the earliest football clubs in Romania, founded in 1906 and based initially in Ploiești before later being relocated to Bucharest. The club was created with the involvement of foreign workers from the oil industry in the Prahova Valley, which gave it a unique international character for its time. It is considered one of the pioneering teams in Romanian football, active during the very early development of organized competitions in the country.

The club’s most important achievement came in the early era of Romanian football when it competed in the national championship and won the title in the 1914–15 season. During this period, Româno-Americană stood out as one of the strongest teams in the country, benefiting from experienced players, many of whom were foreign workers. Their success marked an important moment in the formation of competitive football in Romania and helped shape the structure of early national tournaments.

After World War I began, the club’s activity declined significantly, and it was ultimately dissolved in 1916. Despite its short existence, Româno-Americană București left a lasting historical mark as one of the first champions of Romanian football and a representative of the sport’s formative years in the country. Its legacy is mainly remembered for its pioneering role and early contribution to Romanian football development.

name: FC Progresul București
content:
FC Progresul București was a Romanian football club based in Bucharest, founded in 1944 as the team of the National Bank of Romania. Originally known as BNR București, the club quickly progressed through the Romanian football system and established itself as a stable presence in the top divisions. It was known for its association with educated and urban supporters and was often considered different from the major state-backed clubs of the communist era. Over time, the club also became known under the name Progresul Finanțe Bănci before adopting the simpler Progresul identity.

The club spent many seasons in Romania’s top division and had several notable achievements, including three runner-up finishes in the national league and winning the Romanian Cup in the 1959–60 season. Progresul was also known for its competitive performances in domestic cup competitions, reaching several finals over the decades. Although it never became a dominant force like some of the country’s biggest clubs, it maintained a reputation as a technically solid and respected team that could challenge stronger opponents on its day.

In the 2000s, Progresul București faced serious financial and organizational problems, which led to instability and eventual decline. In 2009, the club was excluded from professional competitions and declared bankrupt, marking the end of its existence in its original form. Despite this, its legacy remains important in Romanian football history, and its identity has inspired later attempts to revive the spirit of the club through successor teams and supporter initiatives.

name: FC Victoria Cluj
content:
FC Victoria Cluj was a Romanian football club based in Cluj-Napoca with a long and fragmented history. It was originally founded in 1920 through a merger involving local student and community teams, making it one of the early football projects in the city. In its early decades, the club competed under different names and represented the Mănăștur neighbourhood, taking part in the first organized Romanian football competitions during the interwar period.

During the 1920s, Victoria Cluj became one of the stronger provincial sides in Romania, reaching multiple national finals but often finishing as runner-up to dominant teams such as Chinezul Timișoara. It also participated in early editions of the national championship structure and went through several identity changes, including competing under the name România Cluj for a period. The club experienced its most competitive era before World War II, when it was regularly present in top-level Romanian football.

After World War II, the club’s activity declined significantly, and it eventually disappeared from professional football in 1947. It was briefly revived in 2019 as a modern project in the lower leagues, but this version also lasted only a few years before being dissolved again in 2022. Despite its instability, Victoria Cluj is remembered as one of the historic early clubs of Cluj football, representing the city’s early contribution to the development of the sport in Romania.

name: FC Politehnica Timișoara
content:
FC Politehnica Timișoara is one of the most well-known football clubs from western Romania, based in the city of Timișoara. The club was founded in 1921 by the Polytechnic University of Timișoara and has long been associated with the academic and student community. Over its early decades, Politehnica developed as a steady presence in Romanian football, often competing in the top divisions but facing strong local rivals such as Ripensia and Chinezul, who were dominant in the interwar period.

The club experienced its most notable sporting achievements in the mid-20th century and later decades, including winning the Romanian Cup twice (1958 and 1980). It also had several strong league campaigns, finishing as runner-up in Liga I on multiple occasions, and became known for producing talented players and competitive teams. In European competitions, Politehnica recorded memorable results against well-known clubs, helping to build its reputation beyond Romania, even though it never managed to win the national league title.

In the 2000s, the club reached another peak but also entered a period of instability due to financial problems and administrative disputes. Despite finishing near the top of the league in the late 2000s and early 2010s, Politehnica was eventually relegated and dissolved in 2012. After its disappearance, several successor projects and re-foundations attempted to continue its legacy. Today, FC Politehnica Timișoara remains a symbol of tradition and strong fan culture in Romanian football, even though the original club no longer exists in its former form.

name: Bukarester FC
content:
Bukarester FC was a Romanian football club based in Bucharest, founded in 1912. It was one of the early teams in the capital and was established mainly by German workers living and working in the city. The club played an important role in the very early development of organized football in Romania and was among the first clubs to compete in the country’s official championship system.

During its short existence, Bukarester FC competed in the Romanian top division in the pre–World War I era and was consistently one of the strongest teams of that time. The club finished as runner-up in the national championship on several occasions, regularly challenging the leading sides of early Romanian football. It was known for having a squad made largely of foreign workers, which influenced its playing style and identity.

After the outbreak of World War I, many foreign players left Romania, which severely weakened the club. Bukarester FC gradually lost its competitiveness and was eventually dissolved in 1916. Despite its short history, it remains an important part of Romanian football’s foundation period and is remembered as one of the pioneer clubs that helped establish the sport in Bucharest.

name: Vagonul Arad
content:
Vagonul Arad was a Romanian football club based in the city of Arad, founded in 1911 and closely connected to the local railway car manufacturing industry. The club was created through the merger of workers’ sports associations linked to the Astra wagon factory, which also inspired its identity and long-standing nickname “the Wagoners.” It quickly became one of the notable teams in Arad’s early football scene and regularly competed in Romania’s developing national competitions.

During its history, Vagonul Arad experienced several periods in Romania’s top divisions, including appearances in Liga I, where its best league result was a second-place finish in the mid-1930s. The club also had a strong presence in cup competitions, reaching the semi-finals of the Romanian Cup and spending many seasons alternating between the first, second, and third tiers of Romanian football. Over time, it went through numerous name changes and reorganizations, reflecting financial and structural instability common for industrial clubs of that era.

In its later years, Vagonul Arad gradually declined and spent most of its time in lower divisions, eventually disappearing from professional football. After multiple mergers and rebrandings during the 20th century, the club was officially dissolved in 2006 following relegation to the lower leagues. Despite its disappearance, it remains part of Arad’s rich football tradition and is remembered as one of the city’s historic industrial-era clubs.

name: FC Sportul Studențesc
content:
FC Sportul Studențesc București is a historic Romanian football club based in Bucharest, founded in 1916 by students and professors under the name Sporting Club Universitar. From its early years, the club was closely linked to academic life and student culture, which became a defining part of its identity. It is considered one of the oldest football institutions in Romania and played an important role in the early development of organized sport in the country.

Throughout its history, Sportul Studențesc experienced several distinct periods, including early participation in national competitions, disappearance during the early communist era, and later revival. The club is best known for its strong emphasis on developing young talent rather than relying on expensive transfers. During the 1970s and 1980s, Sportul reached its peak, consistently competing in Romania’s top division and producing many technically skilled players who later became important figures in Romanian football.

In its most successful era, especially in the 1980s, Sportul achieved its highest league finish (runner-up in the mid-1980s) and regularly competed in European competitions such as the UEFA Cup. It also reached the final of the Balkans Cup and recorded some of its most memorable performances during this period. However, after 1990 the club struggled financially, lost many key players, and gradually declined, eventually dropping out of top-level football and entering long-term instability.

name: FC Vaslui
content:
FC Vaslui is a Romanian football club based in the city of Vaslui, founded in 2002 after the relocation and reorganisation of a lower-division team. The project was created with the goal of quickly building a competitive side capable of reaching the top tiers of Romanian football. Backed by significant financial support in its early years, the club rose rapidly through the divisions, achieving multiple promotions in a short period and reaching Liga I only a few years after its formation.

After establishing itself in Romania’s top division, FC Vaslui became one of the more competitive sides in the league during the late 2000s and early 2010s. The club regularly fought for European qualification spots and was known for signing experienced domestic and international players. Despite strong league performances and participation in UEFA competitions such as the Europa League, Vaslui never managed to win a major domestic trophy, although it often finished near the top of the standings.

The club’s decline began due to financial instability and internal management problems, which eventually led to its collapse. After the main investor withdrew support, FC Vaslui could no longer sustain its squad and operations, resulting in dissolution in 2014. In the following years, several attempts were made to continue football in the city through new projects, but none fully replicated the success of the original club.

name: SR Brașov
content:
SR Brașov is a Romanian football club based in the city of Brașov, founded in 2017 by supporters after the dissolution of the historic FC Brașov. The club was created as a fan-owned project with the goal of continuing the football tradition in the city under the name “Steagul Roșu,” a historic identity closely linked to Brașov football. It started from the lower leagues and was built on community involvement, local support, and a strong desire to preserve the city’s football heritage.

In its early years, SR Brașov competed in the lower tiers of Romanian football and quickly became one of the more followed supporter-run clubs in the country. The team achieved promotion from the county leagues and established itself in Liga III, where it has been competing regularly. The club is known for its passionate fanbase, who actively participate in its management and strongly identify with the traditional colors and symbols of Brașov football.

SR Brașov also emerged in a complex local football landscape where multiple clubs claimed the legacy of the old FC Brașov, leading to divided support in the city. Despite these challenges, SR Brașov has maintained a stable identity as a supporter-owned team and continues to aim for sporting progression while keeping its focus on tradition and community involvement in Romanian football.

name: CFR Timișoara
content:
CSF CFR Timișoara is a Romanian football club based in Timișoara, with origins connected to railway workers and the city’s long football tradition. The club was originally founded in 1919 under the name Sparta CFR Timișoara and later went through several mergers and reorganizations before being re-established in its modern form in 1933. From its early years, it represented the working-class railway community and became one of the traditional sports institutions in the city.

During the mid-20th century, CFR Timișoara experienced its strongest sporting period. The club competed in Romania’s top division and achieved its best historical result in the 1947–48 season, when it finished as runner-up in the national league and also reached the final of the Romanian Cup. In both competitions, it was defeated by ITA Arad, but the season remains the peak of the club’s achievements.

In the following decades, CFR Timișoara became a classic “yo-yo” club, moving between divisions and undergoing several name and structural changes, including the period when it was known as Locomotiva. Despite occasional promotions back to the top flight, the club struggled with instability and financial difficulties, eventually dropping into lower leagues.

name: CSM Jiul Petroșani
content:
CSM Jiul Petroșani is a Romanian football club based in Petroșani, Hunedoara County, strongly connected to the mining history of the Jiu Valley. The club was founded in 1919 under the name CAM Petroșani (Clubul Atletic al Minerilor), reflecting its origins among coal miners and industrial workers. From the beginning, Jiul became one of the oldest and most traditional clubs in Romanian football, representing a region where mining played a central role in community life.

Throughout its history, Jiul Petroșani spent many seasons in Romania’s top two divisions and became known as a classic “yo-yo club,” moving between promotion and relegation. Its most notable achievements include finishing as runner-up in the Romanian top division in the 1924–25 season and winning the Romanian Cup in 1974. The club also reached the final of the Balkans Cup in the late 1970s and participated in European competition, including the European Cup Winners’ Cup in the 1970s.

In later decades, especially after 1990, the club faced serious difficulties as the decline of the mining industry in the Jiu Valley led to financial instability and repeated crises. Jiul struggled with relegations, administrative problems, and near-bankruptcy situations, spending long periods outside the top tier. Despite these challenges, it has survived in various forms and continues to exist in lower divisions, remaining an important symbol of football tradition in the region and one of Romania’s historic industrial clubs.

name: Cercul Atletic București
content:
Cercul Atletic București was an early Romanian football club based in Bucharest, founded around 1912–1913. It was created by members associated with the Athletic Academy of Bucharest and was part of the first generation of organized football teams in Romania. The club represented the early amateur era of Romanian football, when the sport was still developing and largely influenced by foreign players and academic or sporting institutions.

Cercul Atletic București was an early Romanian football club based in Bucharest, founded around 1912–1913. It was created by members associated with the Athletic Academy of Bucharest and was part of the first generation of organized football teams in Romania. The club represented the early amateur era of Romanian football, when the sport was still developing and largely influenced by foreign players and academic or sporting institutions.

After its short participation in official competitions, the club disappeared in the mid-1910s, likely due to the impact of World War I and the instability of early football organizations. Despite its brief existence, Cercul Atletic București is remembered as one of the pioneer clubs in Romanian football history, representing the formative years of the sport in the capital and its early transition toward organized national competition.

name: ASA Târgu Mureș
content:
ASA Târgu Mureș 1962 is a Romanian football club based in Târgu Mureș, founded in 1962 as Asociația Sportivă Armata Târgu Mureș. The club was originally linked to the Romanian Army and was later supported by the Ministry of National Defence, which gave it a relatively strong institutional background during the communist period. In 1964 it absorbed local football structures from Mureșul Târgu Mureș, helping it become the main representative team of the city.

The club experienced its strongest period in the 1970s, when it became one of the competitive sides in Romanian football. Its best league performance came in the 1974–75 season, when it finished as runner-up in Liga I, and it also reached important stages in domestic cup competitions. During this era, ASA was known for being a solid, well-organized team and even took part in European competitions, although without major progress in those tournaments.

After the fall of communism, ASA Târgu Mureș gradually declined due to financial instability and loss of institutional support. The club eventually went bankrupt and was dissolved in 2005 after many seasons outside the top level. Although the original team disappeared, its legacy remained important in the city, later inspiring several re-founded projects that tried to continue the football tradition in Târgu Mureș.

name: ASA 2013 Târgu Mureș
content:
ASA 2013 Târgu Mureș was a Romanian football club based in Târgu Mureș, created in 2008 under the name FCM Târgu Mureș and later rebranded in 2013. The club was part of a project to revive top-level football in the city after earlier historic teams had disappeared. It gradually rose through the Romanian football league system, quickly becoming the main representative of Târgu Mureș in professional football.

The club reached its peak in the mid-2010s after gaining promotion to Liga I, where it surprisingly became one of the strongest sides in Romania. In the 2014–15 season, ASA Târgu Mureș finished as runner-up in the national championship, narrowly missing out on the title after a dramatic final round. This period also brought international competition, as the club qualified for the UEFA Europa League and faced AS Saint-Étienne in European qualifiers.

Shortly after its success, the club entered a rapid decline due to serious financial problems and instability. Despite winning the Romanian Supercup in 2015, ASA could not maintain its level and soon dropped back down the divisions. In 2018, the club was dissolved after withdrawing from professional competition, ending a short but memorable period in Romanian football history.

name: CS Pandurii Târgu Jiu
content:
CS Pandurii Târgu Jiu was a Romanian football club based in the city of Târgu Jiu, founded in 1962 through the merger of two local teams. The club represented the Gorj region and was strongly associated with the local mining industry, which also influenced its identity and nickname. For most of its early history, Pandurii competed in the lower divisions of Romanian football, gradually building its structure and gaining experience before reaching higher levels of competition.

The club’s rise began in the 2000s, when it achieved promotion to Liga I for the first time in 2005. After establishing itself in the top division, Pandurii steadily improved its performances, finishing mid-table in several seasons and becoming a stable first-division team. Its biggest success came in the 2012–13 season, when the club finished as runner-up in Liga I, which marked the highest achievement in its history and earned qualification for European competitions, including the UEFA Europa League.

Following its peak, Pandurii faced serious financial problems that led to instability, loss of key players, and rapid decline. The club eventually dropped through the divisions in the following years, struggling to maintain professional status. Despite attempts to recover, CS Pandurii Târgu Jiu was ultimately dissolved in 2022, ending its run as one of the notable modern clubs from Romania’s Oltenia region.

name: FC Carmen București
content:
FC Carmen București is a Romanian football club based in Bucharest, originally founded in 1922. The club was created by businessman Ionel Mociorniță and quickly became one of the stronger teams in Romanian football during the interwar period. Carmen was known for its professional organization and ability to attract some of the best players of the era, making it a competitive side in the early national championships.

The club’s peak came in the 1946–47 season, when it finished as runner-up in Romania’s top division, narrowly missing out on the title. During this period, Carmen was considered one of the most powerful teams in the country, competing closely with other top clubs of the time. However, its strong position also placed it in conflict with the political changes happening in Romania after World War II.

In 1947, the communist authorities dissolved FC Carmen București, and its place in Romanian football was removed as part of wider restructuring of sports clubs under the new regime. The club remained inactive for decades until it was re-founded in modern times, attempting to revive its historical identity. Despite its short original existence, Carmen remains remembered as one of the prominent pre-war clubs and an example of how politics influenced football history in Romania.

name: Societatea Gimnastică Sibiu
content:
Societatea Gimnastică Sibiu was a historic sports club based in Sibiu, founded in 1919 as a football section of a much older German gymnastic society that dated back to the 19th century. The club emerged in a multicultural environment where Saxon, Hungarian, and Romanian communities all influenced local sport development. After World War I, it became one of the early football teams representing Sibiu in the newly formed Romanian competitions and quickly joined the national football structure.

During the interwar period, the club achieved its most significant results in Romanian football. It competed in the national championship and reached its peak in the 1930–31 season, when it finished as runner-up after losing the final to UDR Reșița. This remains the club’s greatest sporting achievement and marked it as one of the strongest provincial teams of its time, capable of challenging established clubs in Romanian football.

After this successful period, Societatea Gimnastică Sibiu gradually declined in performance and importance. The club continued to participate in Romanian competitions for several more years but was unable to maintain its earlier level of success. Eventually, it disappeared after World War II in 1945, ending its existence as one of the historic early football institutions of Sibiu and leaving behind a legacy tied to the foundations of Romanian football development.

name: AFC Gloria Arad
content:
AFC Gloria Arad is a Romanian football club based in the city of Arad, with origins dating back to 1913. It was founded as Gloria Arad and quickly became one of the early football teams in the region, representing one of the oldest sporting traditions in western Romania. The club’s identity has historically been linked with the city’s industrial and working-class background, and it played an important role in the early development of Romanian football during the interwar period.

One of the club’s most notable achievements came in the early era of Romanian football, when it finished as runner-up in the national championship in the 1929–30 season. In the following decades, Gloria Arad spent much of its history moving between divisions, experiencing both periods of higher-level competition and long stretches in lower leagues. Despite financial and organizational difficulties over time, the club remained a recognizable name in Arad’s football landscape.

In modern times, the club went through several reorganizations, bankruptcies, and re-foundations, reflecting the instability common among historic Romanian teams. It was eventually re-established in the 2020s by supporters and local stakeholders aiming to revive the traditional identity of Gloria Arad. Today, AFC Gloria Arad continues to operate in the lower divisions, focusing on rebuilding its sporting structure while preserving its long historical legacy in Romanian football.

name: ACS Minerul Lupeni
content:
ACS Minerul Lupeni is a Romanian football club based in Lupeni, Hunedoara County, a city strongly tied to the mining industry of the Jiu Valley. The club originally traces its roots back to 1920, when it was founded under the name Jiul Lupeni as a workers’ team representing the local mining community. Over time, the club went through several name changes and reorganizations, most notably becoming Minerul Lupeni, a name that reflects its deep connection to the region’s coal mining identity.

Throughout its history, Minerul Lupeni has mostly competed in the lower divisions of Romanian football, but it also experienced important periods of success. One of its early highlights came in the interwar era, when the team reached the final of the national championship in the 1927–28 season, finishing as runner-up after losing to Colțea Brașov. In later decades, the club fluctuated between divisions, including spells in Liga II and Liga III, reflecting both competitive ambition and the financial limitations typical of mining-town clubs.

In the modern era, the club has faced instability, including dissolution in 2010 and later revival efforts by local authorities and supporters. It was re-established in the 2020s and continues to compete in lower leagues while trying to rebuild its sporting structure and identity. Despite its ups and downs, ACS Minerul Lupeni remains an important symbol of the Jiu Valley’s football tradition and working-class heritage, maintaining a loyal local following.

name: ACF Gloria Bistrița
content:
ACF Gloria Bistrița is a Romanian football club based in the city of Bistrița, founded in 1922. The club became one of the most important sporting institutions in the region and spent much of its history developing within the Romanian football system. It traditionally represented the city in national competitions and became strongly associated with the white and blue colors that defined its identity. The club grew steadily over the decades, moving between lower divisions before eventually reaching the top level of Romanian football.

The most successful period in the club’s history came after its promotion to the first division in 1990. During this era, Gloria Bistrița established itself as a solid Liga I team, often finishing in the upper half of the table and competing against Romania’s strongest clubs. The highlight of its achievements was winning the Romanian Cup in 1994, which also gave the club access to European competition. It later participated in continental tournaments, gaining experience against stronger international opponents and building its reputation as a competitive mid-table team.

In the 2000s and early 2010s, the club gradually declined due to financial problems and administrative instability. Despite attempts to stabilize its performance, Gloria struggled to maintain its top-flight status and was eventually relegated. The original club was declared bankrupt and dissolved in 2015, ending a long chapter in Romanian football history. However, its legacy continued through successor projects and new clubs in Bistrița that aimed to preserve its tradition and identity.

name: FC Electroputere Craiova
content:
FC Electroputere Craiova was a Romanian football club based in the city of Craiova, historically linked to the large industrial company Electroputere. The club was founded in 1949 under different names and gradually became known as Electroputere Craiova, reflecting its connection to the local factory workforce. Like many Eastern European “works teams,” it represented an industrial enterprise and played an important role in regional football culture during the communist era.

The team spent much of its early history moving between the second and third tiers of Romanian football, but it reached its peak in the early 1990s. During this period, Electroputere Craiova earned promotion to the top division and achieved its best-ever finish by placing third in the Romanian first league in the 1991–92 season. This strong performance allowed the club to qualify for European competition, where it competed in the UEFA Cup but was eliminated in the early rounds.

After its brief success, the club struggled to maintain stability in the top flight and gradually declined. It changed names several times in the late 1990s, including Extensiv Craiova, before eventually losing its place in higher-level Romanian football. By the early 2000s, the original club structure had effectively disappeared, and its legacy was later continued through other local teams such as FC Caracal after relocation and rebranding.

name: Victoria București
content:
Victoria București was a Romanian football club based in Bucharest, founded in 1949. Throughout most of its existence, the club was closely linked to the Romanian Ministry of Internal Affairs (the police system) and functioned as one of several state-associated teams during the communist era. Over the years, it went through multiple name changes and spent much of its early history in the lower divisions of Romanian football before gradually rising in competitiveness.

The club reached its peak in the mid to late 1980s after gaining promotion to the top division in 1985. Victoria quickly became one of the stronger teams in Romania, consistently finishing near the top of the league, including several consecutive third-place finishes behind dominant clubs like Steaua București and Dinamo București. It also participated in European competitions, including the UEFA Cup, where it achieved moderate success and reached the quarter-finals in the 1988–89 season.

Despite its on-field success, Victoria București became widely associated with controversy, including allegations of political influence and unfair advantages due to its connections with the Ministry of Internal Affairs. Following the Romanian Revolution in 1989 and the collapse of the communist system, the club lost its backing and was officially dissolved in early 1990.

name: FC Corvinul Hunedoara
content:
FC Corvinul Hunedoara is a Romanian football club based in the city of Hunedoara, originally founded in 1921. The club has gone through several name changes and reorganizations over its long history, reflecting different political and industrial periods in Romania. It is closely associated with the city’s steel industry and the symbolic heritage of the Corvin family, from which it also takes its name.

The club experienced its most successful period in the 1980s, when it competed regularly in Romania’s top division and became known for developing talented players and playing attractive football. Under the management of Mircea Lucescu, Corvinul achieved strong league performances, including a third-place finish in the early 1980s, and qualified for European competitions such as the UEFA Cup. Several players from this era went on to represent the Romanian national team or play abroad.

After the fall of communism, Corvinul declined significantly and was relegated from the top flight in 1992, never returning to the highest level. Financial problems and structural changes eventually led to instability, and the club lost its professional status in the 2000s. However, the Corvinul identity was later revived and re-established in the 2020s, continuing its legacy in Romanian football and rebuilding its presence in the national league system.

name: CA Câmpulung Moldovenesc
content:
CA Câmpulung Moldovenesc was a Romanian football club based in Câmpulung Moldovenesc, in the Bukovina region. The club was originally formed in 1948 under the name CS Armata in Iași as a military-associated sports team representing the Romanian army. It initially competed in the lower divisions and gradually progressed through the national league system during the late 1940s and early 1950s.

In 1951, the club was relocated to Câmpulung Moldovenesc and renamed CA Câmpulung Moldovenesc. This move marked the beginning of its most successful period, as the team quickly achieved promotion to Romania’s top division. The club was able to strengthen its squad and compete at a high level despite its short existence in the top flight.

The peak of CA Câmpulung Moldovenesc came in the early 1950s, when it secured a strong third-place finish in the national league in 1952 and was even leading the championship halfway through the 1953 season. However, despite this success, the club was abruptly disbanded in 1953. Its players were redistributed to other teams, including major Romanian clubs, marking the end of its brief but notable presence in Romanian football.

name: Colțea București
content:
Colțea București was one of the earliest Romanian football clubs, based in Bucharest and founded in 1913. It was created as part of a sports association linked to the Colțea Hospital, which also influenced its name. In the early years of Romanian football, the club quickly became one of the prominent teams in the capital and played an important role in the development of the sport in the country.

The club achieved its greatest success during the 1910s and early 1920s, when Romanian football was still in its formative stage. Colțea București won the national championship in the 1915–16 season and again in 1919–20, establishing itself as one of the strongest teams of the pre-professional era. During this period, the national competition was structured in a knockout format with regional champions, and Colțea consistently performed well against other leading clubs of the time.

After the early 1920s, the club’s influence began to decline as new, more powerful teams emerged in Bucharest and other cities. Colțea București gradually lost competitiveness and eventually disappeared from top-level Romanian football. Despite its later obscurity, the club is remembered as one of the pioneers of the sport in Romania and an early multiple-time national champion.

name: Sepsi OSK
content:
Sepsi OSK Sfântu Gheorghe is a Romanian professional football club based in Sfântu Gheorghe, Covasna County. Founded in 2011, the club experienced a remarkably fast rise through the Romanian football league system, earning promotion from the fifth division to Liga I within only six years. Sepsi became the first club from Covasna County to compete in Romania’s top football division, gaining attention for representing the Székely Hungarian community in the region.

The club is known for its red and white colors, chosen to honor the football traditions of the city, and plays its home matches at the modern Sepsi Arena. Under the ownership of businessman László Diószegi, Sepsi invested heavily in infrastructure and youth development, receiving support from sponsors and financial backing connected to the Hungarian community. The team quickly established itself as a competitive side in Romanian football, regularly challenging stronger and more historic clubs.

Sepsi OSK achieved its greatest success in the early 2020s by winning the Cupa României in consecutive seasons in 2022 and 2023, as well as lifting the Romanian Super Cup twice. These victories allowed the club to participate in European competitions and further increased its reputation both in Romania and abroad. Despite being a relatively young club, Sepsi has become one of the most recognizable modern football projects in Romanian football.

name: FC Voluntari
content:
FC Voluntari is a Romanian professional football club based in Voluntari, Ilfov County, near Bucharest. Founded in 2010, the club experienced a rapid rise through the Romanian football league system, earning consecutive promotions from Liga III to Liga I within a few seasons. Their fast development made them one of the newest clubs to reach the top division of Romanian football.

The team plays its home matches at the Anghel Iordănescu Stadium, named after the famous Romanian coach and former national team manager. Although FC Voluntari is a relatively young club with a smaller fanbase compared to traditional Romanian teams, it became known for maintaining stability in Liga I for many years. The club is owned by the town of Voluntari and has often focused on experienced Romanian players and coaches.

FC Voluntari achieved the greatest success in its history during the 2016–17 season, when it won the Cupa României after defeating Astra Giurgiu in the final. Shortly afterward, the club also won the Supercupa României, securing two major domestic trophies in a short period. Despite later being relegated to Liga II after the 2023–24 season, FC Voluntari remains recognized as one of the most successful newly founded clubs in modern Romanian football.

name: CFR Turnu Severin
content:
CFR Turnu Severin is a historic Romanian football club based in Drobeta-Turnu Severin, founded in 1928. Originally established as a railway workers’ team, the club became one of the most respected sides in Romanian football during the pre-war and wartime years. It gained national recognition after winning the Romanian Cup in 1943, one of the greatest achievements in the club’s history and a remarkable success for a team from a smaller city.

During the 1940s and 1950s, CFR Turnu Severin competed in Romania’s top lower divisions and was close to becoming a stronger presence in the national championship. The club earned promotion to the top tier in the early 1940s, but the outbreak of World War II interrupted the regular competition schedule. After the war, the team continued to play under different names linked to Romania’s railway system, but gradually declined and was dissolved in 1958.

For decades the club disappeared from Romanian football, while other teams carried the sporting tradition of the city. In 2018, CFR Turnu Severin was officially re-founded, bringing back one of the oldest football identities in the region. Since its return, the club has competed in local county leagues, aiming to rebuild its reputation while honoring its historical legacy as one of Romania’s classic railway football clubs.

name: ACS Sticla Arieșul Turda
content:
ACS Sticla Arieșul Turda is a Romanian football club based in the city of Turda, Cluj County. The club continues the long football tradition of the area, particularly connected with the historic teams Sticla Turda and Arieșul Turda. Over the decades, football in Turda has played an important role in local sports culture, with the club representing the city in various levels of the Romanian league system.

The team was formed through the merger and continuation of local football organizations after financial difficulties affected previous clubs from Turda. By combining the identities of Sticla and Arieșul, the club aimed to preserve the football heritage of the city while rebuilding a competitive structure for the future. ACS Sticla Arieșul Turda mainly competed in the lower divisions of Romanian football, focusing on local talent development and maintaining community support.

Throughout its history, the club has been recognized for its connection to the industrial and sporting traditions of Turda. Although it has not achieved major national success, ACS Sticla Arieșul Turda remains an important symbol of local football identity in Cluj County. The club reflects the persistence of smaller Romanian football communities that continue to preserve their sporting traditions despite financial and competitive challenges.

name: Chimia Râmnicu Vâlcea
content:
Chimia Râmnicu Vâlcea was a Romanian football club based in Râmnicu Vâlcea, founded in 1946. Throughout its history, the club changed its name several times before becoming widely known as Chimia Râmnicu Vâlcea in 1967. The team represented one of the most important football institutions in Vâlcea County and spent many seasons competing in the upper levels of Romanian football.

The greatest achievement in the club’s history came during the 1972–73 season, when Chimia won the Cupa României despite playing in the second division. This remarkable success earned the club qualification for the 1973–74 European Cup Winners’ Cup, where it faced Glentoran from Northern Ireland. Shortly after the cup triumph, the team gained promotion to Romania’s top division and enjoyed one of its strongest periods during the late 1970s and 1980s, spending several consecutive seasons in Divizia A.

After years of decline and financial difficulties, the club gradually fell through the Romanian league system during the 1990s. In 1994 it changed its name to FC Râmnicu Vâlcea, but the problems continued, eventually leading to its dissolution in 2004. Despite disappearing from professional football, Chimia Râmnicu Vâlcea remains remembered as one of the most respected traditional clubs from southern Romania, especially for its historic Romanian Cup victory and long-standing contribution to local football culture.

name: CS Minaur Baia Mare
content:
CS Minaur Baia Mare is a Romanian football club based in Baia Mare, Maramureș County, and is part of the wider sports society CS Minaur Baia Mare. The football section traces its roots back to 1948, when the original club was founded under the name CSM Baia Mare. Over the decades, the team went through numerous name changes and reorganizations, often reflecting shifts in sponsorship, local industry influence, and financial stability. Despite these changes, the club remained an important representative of football in northern Romania.

Throughout its history, Minaur Baia Mare spent most of its existence in Romania’s second tier, with several periods in the top division. The club experienced its strongest era in the late 1970s and early 1980s, when it regularly competed in Liga I and even achieved notable performances in domestic cup competitions. During these years, it became known for producing talented players and for its competitive matches against some of Romania’s stronger teams, establishing a solid regional football identity.

In modern times, the club has faced financial difficulties, including bankruptcies and multiple re-foundations, most recently being re-established in 2017 under the Minaur name. Since then, it has competed mainly in the lower divisions, working to rebuild stability and return to higher levels of Romanian football. Despite its ups and downs, CS Minaur Baia Mare remains a symbol of football tradition in Maramureș and continues to carry the legacy of one of the region’s most historic clubs.

name: FC Hermannstadt
content:
FC Hermannstadt is a Romanian professional football club based in Sibiu, founded in 2015. The club was created to continue the long football tradition of the city, which had been represented over the years by several earlier teams. Although it is not the legal successor of any previous club, Hermannstadt is widely seen as the modern sporting representative of Sibiu in national competitions. The club quickly started its journey in the lower leagues and built its identity around rapid development and strong local support.

After its foundation, FC Hermannstadt achieved a remarkable rise through the Romanian football system. Starting in Liga IV, the team won promotion almost immediately and continued its progression through Liga III and Liga II in consecutive seasons. This rapid ascent allowed the club to reach Liga I in 2018, just a few years after being established. In the same period, Hermannstadt also made a surprising run in the Cupa României, reaching the final despite being a newly promoted side and defeating several top-division opponents along the way.

Since reaching the top tier, FC Hermannstadt has established itself as a stable Liga I club, often finishing mid-table and focusing on consolidation rather than title challenges. The team plays its home matches at the Municipal Stadium in Sibiu and continues to develop its squad with a mix of experienced players and young talents. Hermannstadt remains an important symbol of modern football revival in Sibiu and is recognized for its fast rise and competitive performances against more established Romanian clubs.

name: CAM Timișoara
content:
CAM Timișoara was a Romanian football club based in Timișoara, formed in 1936 as a result of the merger between Club Atletic Timișoara (CA Timișoara) and RGM Timișoara. Both predecessor clubs had long traditions in regional football dating back to the early 20th century. The merger created a new identity intended to strengthen the city’s representation in national competitions, and the club became one of the notable teams in western Romania during the interwar and early post-war periods.

During its existence, CAM Timișoara competed mainly in Divizia B, but it also had periods in the top tier of Romanian football. One of its most significant achievements came in the late 1930s, when the team reached strong league positions and also made a remarkable run in the Cupa României final while still being a second-division side. The club eventually earned promotion to Divizia A and competed at the highest level for a short period, where it faced some of the strongest Romanian teams of that era.

After World War II, CAM Timișoara went through several reorganizations and temporary mergers, including a brief period linked with Chinezul Timișoara. Despite these efforts, the club struggled with instability and declining results.
