By the late 1940s, it was relegated to lower divisions, and in 1949 the club was dissolved, marking the end of its existence. Nevertheless, CAM Timișoara remains an important part of the early football history of Timișoara, a city known for its strong sporting traditions.

name: CS Gaz Metan Mediaș
content:
CS Gaz Metan Mediaș was a Romanian professional football club based in Mediaș, Sibiu County, founded in 1945 under the name Karres Mediaș. Over its early years, the club went through multiple name changes and reorganizations linked to local industry and ownership transitions, eventually becoming Gaz Metan Mediaș later in the late 1940s. It was historically supported by the local gas industry, which also influenced its identity and development. The club became one of the main football representatives of the city of Mediaș.

Throughout its history, Gaz Metan Mediaș spent most of its seasons in Romania’s second division but also had significant periods in Liga I, the country’s top tier, where it played a total of 16 seasons. One of its most notable early achievements was reaching the final of the Cupa României in 1951, where it finished as runner-up. The club’s modern peak came in the 2011–12 season when it competed in European football for the first time, reaching the UEFA Europa League play-off round after eliminating stronger opponents such as KuPS and Mainz 05.

In its later years, the club experienced financial instability and declining results, which eventually led to its dissolution in 2022. Despite this, Gaz Metan Mediaș remained a respected name in Romanian football, known for its resilience, occasional strong cup runs, and ability to compete at the highest level despite limited resources. After its disappearance, efforts emerged locally to continue the football tradition in Mediaș through successor projects, preserving its sporting legacy.

name: CSM Câmpia Turzii
content:
CSM Câmpia Turzii is a Romanian football club based in Câmpia Turzii, Cluj County. The club traces its origins back to 1921, when it was founded under the name Industria Sârmei Câmpia Turzii, reflecting the city’s strong industrial background. Over the decades, the team became one of the most traditional football institutions in the region, going through multiple name changes while maintaining its local identity and presence in Romanian football.

Throughout its history, the club experienced both notable successes and long periods in lower divisions. Its peak moments came in the mid-20th century, when it reached Romania’s top division and even played in Divizia A, while also achieving strong runs in domestic competitions such as the Romanian Cup, including a final appearance. However, most of its existence was spent in the second and third tiers, where it remained a competitive but unstable presence, often affected by financial and organizational changes.

In the modern era, the club struggled with financial instability, frequent rebrandings, and repeated dissolutions and refoundations. After several attempts to restart under different names, the team was ultimately dissolved in 2021. Despite this, CSM Câmpia Turzii is still remembered as one of the historic industrial clubs of Romanian football, representing the sporting tradition of its city for nearly a century.

name: Siderurgistul Galați
content:
Siderurgistul Galați was a Romanian football club based in Galați, founded in 1955 under the name Dinamo Galați. Over the following years, the club underwent several reorganizations and name changes, becoming CSO Galați and later adopting the name Siderurgistul in 1962. The team was closely connected to the local industrial environment, particularly the steel industry, which influenced both its identity and development.

The club experienced its strongest period in the early 1960s. In 1963, Siderurgistul achieved promotion to Divizia A, Romania’s top football division, and also reached the final of the Cupa României, where it finished as runner-up after a heavy defeat against Petrolul Ploiești. Despite these successes, the club struggled to maintain stability at the highest level, finishing low in the league and suffering immediate relegation after its top-flight seasons.

After a brief return to Divizia A in the mid-1960s, Siderurgistul Galați was unable to sustain long-term success. The club continued to fluctuate between divisions but failed to establish itself as a stable top-tier side. In 1967, after finishing second in the second division and undergoing structural changes in local football, the club was dissolved. Despite its short existence, Siderurgistul remains remembered for its rapid rise and its notable cup run in Romanian football history.

name: Foresta Fălticeni
content:
Foresta Fălticeni was a Romanian football club based in Fălticeni, Suceava County, founded in 1954 under the name Avântul Fălticeni. Over time, the club went through several name changes before becoming known as Foresta, reflecting different periods of restructuring and local sponsorship. It became one of the representative teams of the region, competing mainly in the lower divisions of Romanian football while building a strong local identity.

The club’s most notable achievement came in the 1966–67 season, when Foresta Fălticeni reached the final of the Cupa României, a rare success for a lower-division side. In that same era, the team gained national attention for its competitive performances against stronger opposition, even though it ultimately lost the final to a top-tier club. Later in the 1990s, Foresta experienced its golden modern period, achieving promotion to Liga I and competing at the highest level of Romanian football for several seasons.

Foresta also became famous for one of the most dramatic matches in Romanian football history, a remarkable comeback victory against Dinamo București after being 0–4 down. Despite these highlights, the club struggled with financial instability and relocations between Fălticeni and Suceava, which weakened its long-term stability. Eventually, Foresta was dissolved in 2003, but it remains remembered for its historic cup run, top-flight appearances, and unforgettable matches.

name: Constructorul Galați
content:
Constructorul Galați was a Romanian football club based in Galați, founded in 1950. The team represented a working-class, industrial background, and throughout its history it went through several name changes linked to local organizations and industrial sponsors. Despite never becoming one of Romania’s major clubs, it was a stable presence in the country’s lower leagues and occasionally competed at higher levels.

The club’s most successful period came in the early 1970s. In the 1972–73 season, Constructorul Galați achieved a remarkable run in the Cupa României, reaching the final despite being a lower-division side. Along the way, the team produced major surprises by eliminating top Romanian clubs such as Steaua București and Dinamo București, which made their cup run one of the most famous underdog stories in Romanian football history. In the same season, the club also won its Divizia C series, earning promotion to Divizia B.

In the final, Constructorul Galați faced Chimia Râmnicu Vâlcea and finished as runner-up after a replayed match. Despite this historic achievement, the club never managed to build on its success at the top level. In 1975, Constructorul was relocated and transformed into Victoria Tecuci, effectively ending its existence as an independent club, but its 1973 cup run remains a defining moment in its legacy.

name: FCM Dunărea Galați
content:
FCM Dunărea Galați was a Romanian football club based in Galați, founded in 1970. The team was created to represent the city in national competitions and quickly became one of the main football sides in the region. Throughout its existence, the club played its home matches at Stadionul Nicolae Rainea and was known for its blue identity and strong connection to local supporters. It spent most of its history competing between Romania’s top three divisions.

During its peak periods, Dunărea Galați managed to reach Liga I, Romania’s top division, where it played a total of five seasons. The club had several promotions from Liga II and was often considered a strong second-tier side capable of challenging for top-flight football. However, after the rise of Oțelul Galați in the 1980s, Dunărea gradually lost its status as the city’s leading club and spent more time in lower divisions.

In its later years, the club continued to fluctuate between Liga II and Liga III, struggling with instability and inconsistent results. Despite occasional competitive seasons and cup appearances, it was unable to re-establish itself in the top division. Ultimately, FCM Dunărea Galați was dissolved in 2014, ending its long existence but leaving behind a legacy as one of Galați’s historic football teams.

name: FC Olimpia Satu Mare
content:
FC Olimpia Satu Mare is a Romanian football club based in Satu Mare, with origins dating back to 1921. It is one of the older football institutions in Romania and has historically been an important representative of the region. The club became known under the name Olimpia during its long existence and developed a strong local identity, often supported by passionate fan groups. It has spent much of its history moving between different levels of the Romanian football league system.

Throughout its history, Olimpia experienced several notable sporting moments, including early participation in the Romanian Cup and appearances in the top division after league restructurings. The club reached one of its major peaks in the 1970s, when it played in Romania’s top tier and also reached the Romanian Cup final in 1978, where it finished as runner-up. Despite these achievements, Olimpia often struggled with consistency and frequently moved between divisions due to sporting and financial challenges.

In the modern era, FC Olimpia Satu Mare faced serious financial difficulties, leading to relegations and eventual collapse in its original form. After its dissolution, the football tradition in the city continued through successor and supporter-based projects, but legal continuity remained disputed. Today, the Olimpia name still carries historical significance in Satu Mare football, representing both the club’s long legacy and the ongoing efforts to preserve its identity.

name: FCM Bacău
content:
FCM Bacău is a Romanian football club based in Bacău, founded in 1950 under the name Dinamo Bacău. Over the decades, the club underwent several name changes, including Sport Club Bacău and other identities linked to regional and political shifts, before becoming widely known as FCM Bacău. It developed as one of the most important football teams in the Moldavia region and played many seasons in Romania’s top divisions. The club traditionally represented the city in national competitions and built a strong local identity.

The club experienced its strongest period during the 1960s–2000s, when it regularly competed in Divizia A (Liga I). One of its best league performances came in the late 1960s when it finished near the top positions, and it also achieved several solid cup runs. Over its history, FCM Bacău spent more than four decades in the top flight, producing notable players and becoming a stable mid-table team capable of challenging stronger Romanian sides.

In the modern era, the club gradually declined due to financial instability and changes in local football politics. It suffered relegations, reorganizations, and multiple attempts at revival under supporter-led or municipal projects. Despite efforts to maintain its tradition, the original FCM Bacău structure eventually disappeared from professional football. Even so, the club remains an important part of Romanian football history, remembered for its long presence in Liga I and its contribution to the development of players in the region.

name: AFC Dacia Unirea Brăila
content:
AFC Dacia Unirea Brăila is a Romanian football club based in Brăila, founded in 1919, making it one of the oldest football institutions in the country. The club emerged from the merger of early local teams and gradually became the main football representative of the city. Over its long history, it has undergone multiple name changes and reorganizations, reflecting the economic and political shifts in Romania throughout the 20th century. The team traditionally plays its home matches at the Municipal Stadium in Brăila and is closely associated with the city’s sporting identity.

The club has spent most of its existence moving between Romania’s second and third divisions, but it has also had periods in the top flight. One of its most successful eras came in the early 1990s, when Dacia Unirea finished sixth in Divizia A during the 1991–92 season, its best-ever league result. The following season, the club reached the final of the Cupa României, marking its greatest achievement in domestic cup competition. These results established the team as a strong provincial side capable of competing with major Romanian clubs at its peak.

In later years, Dacia Unirea Brăila struggled with financial instability and inconsistent performances, which led to relegations and frequent restructuring. Despite efforts to rebuild and stabilize the club, it was unable to maintain a long-term presence in the top divisions. Today, it continues to compete in the lower leagues, focusing on rebuilding its sporting project and preserving its long-standing tradition as one of the historic football names in Romanian football.

name: AFC Rocar București
content:
AFC Rocar București was a Romanian football club based in Bucharest, founded in 1953. The club originally represented the Autobuzul (bus manufacturing) factory and spent much of its early history under industrial sponsorship. Over time, it went through several name changes, including Autobuzul București and later Rocar București, reflecting shifts in ownership and organization. The team played its home matches at the ANEFS Stadium and built its identity as a small but resilient club from the capital.

The club’s most successful period came at the end of the 1990s and beginning of the 2000s. Rocar achieved promotion to Romania’s top division, Divizia A, in 1999 and competed there for two seasons. Its biggest achievement was reaching the final of the Cupa României in the 2000–01 season, a remarkable run for a modest club that had only recently entered the top flight. During this time, it also developed several players who later moved to more prominent Romanian teams.

After being relegated from the top division in 2001, the club experienced a rapid decline. It spent time in lower leagues, faced financial difficulties, and was eventually restructured as Rocar ANEFS București before disappearing completely. The club was officially dissolved in 2009, but it remains remembered for its short-lived rise to prominence and its surprising cup final run, which stands as the highlight of its history.
